title: Influencers Have a Lot to Say About Politics. Many Are Quietly Paid for It.
partialText: Their videos have proliferated on social media, but the payments are frequently hidden from viewers.

title: El-Sayed Apologizes for March Comment About Michigan Synagogue Attack
partialText: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan, faced criticism from Jewish Democrats after remarking, “hurt people hurt people.”

title: In Georgia, Jon Ossoff Courts Broad Appeal With an Anti-Trump Script for Senate Race
partialText: Senator Jon Ossoff, the youngest sitting senator and the only Democrat seeking re-election this year in a state President Trump won in 2024, hasn’t moderated his message in his critical race.

title: One Democrat to Face Three Republicans for Alaska Governor
partialText: The second-place finisher in a primary where the top four advance to the November ballot said he would drop out of the race so voters could coalesce behind a single Democratic candidate.

title: How Meta’s $17.1 Billion Social Media Settlement Came Together
partialText: State attorneys general spent months in negotiations. Then, as its legal losses mounted, the social media giant’s new top lawyer brought a huge settlement to the table.

title: What’s Changing For Teens on Instagram and Facebook After Meta Settlement
partialText: Meta agreed to set more time limits and enhance protections in its platforms for young users, but was short on some specifics.

title: An ICE Shooting, an Extradition Showdown and the Federal Case That Stalled
partialText: Federal prosecutors planned to charge an immigration agent arrested in connection with a shooting in Minneapolis. Then the agent walked free.

title: How Trump’s Deportation Agenda Spreads Overseas
partialText: Our White House correspondent Zolan Kanno-Youngs explains how so-called third-country deportations are sending immigrants to countries across the globe.

title: Relative of Afghans Who Helped U.S. Military Is Deported to Africa
partialText: The Trump administration has deported thousands of immigrants to countries where they have no ties. Dozens were on the latest flight, to the Central African Republic.

title: Trump Says U.S. Struck Deal for Control of More Than 65 Billion Barrels of Venezuela’s Oil
partialText: The president said an agreement between the countries covered more than 65 billion barrels of reserves. A U.S. official said it would involve a partnership with a private company.

title: Carney Has Canadians’ Support on Trump. Now Comes the Hard Part.
partialText: The U.S.-Canada trade war has galvanized Canadians behind their prime minister’s decision to walk away from negotiations. What happens when the time comes for talks to restart?

title: ‘Lake America’? These Upstate New Yorkers Aren’t Letting Go of ‘Ontario.’
partialText: President Trump on Thursday signed an order rechristening Lake Ontario as Lake America, but businesses around Niagara Falls say they won’t be changing their tune.

title: Judge Rules Trump Unlawfully Targeted Stanford Students Who Criticized Israel
partialText: The ruling was a win for Stanford’s student newspaper, The Stanford Daily, and it followed another court victory for students targeted by the Trump administration last year.

title: Search Continues for 2,400 Missing in Nepal Floods Amid ‘Immense’ Devastation
partialText: As rescue efforts entered their fourth day, the scale of destruction came into focus, signaling a daunting recovery for the vulnerable nation.

title: Catastrophic Flood Exposes the Risks of Nepal’s Hydropower Bet
partialText: The loss of power-generating capacity has raised questions about an ambitious expansion of renewable energy in one of the world’s most hazard-prone mountain regions.

title: Nepali City Struggles to Handle the Many Bodies on Its Riverbanks
partialText: The remains of hundreds of people have washed downstream after devastating floods.

title: Ina Garten Says You Can Either Get on Her Train or Get Out of the Way
partialText: At 78, the cookbook author and Food Network host knows what she likes, knows what she wants and isn’t stopping anytime soon.

title: Democrats Have an Identity Politics Problem. Just Not the One You Think.
partialText: Instead of rallying around their candidates, Democrats are falling out among themselves.

title: We’re in a New Era of Class Warfare. History Points to a Way Out.
partialText: The class-based violence of the past was part of a broader struggle. Today, the violence is the end in itself.

title: Fast Forward
partialText: How do we balance our desire for modern conveniences with our nostalgia for the uncomplicated felicity of our pre-internet past?

title: With Shoppers Wary of Illness, Farmers Destroy Millions of Heads of Lettuce
partialText: After a drop in demand driven by a nationwide outbreak of cyclosporiasis, California growers are plowing lettuce back into the soil and laying off workers.
